prioritized_defects.description: The diagram routes the 'any peering policies exist' branch to a generic final node labeled 'Pass control on' instead of ending in a final node whose label names the long-term peering outcome. Requirement R128 says preexisting peering arrangements / peering policies are returned to establish a long-term peering arrangement, which is the branch-specific outcome, not just generic pass-through control.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R25: 'If there are any preexisting peering arrangements ... then these will be returned at this point.' R128: 'If any peering policies exist, they are returned to establish long-term peering arrangement.' The diagram ends this branch at N18 labeled 'Pass control on'.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Replace the generic final node on the long-term policy-return branch with a final node labeled to name that outcome, such as 'Long-term peering arrangement' or 'Policies returned', so the branch termination matches the requirement.

prioritized_defects.description: The rejection/failure path for insufficient resources ends at the generic final node 'Pass control on' rather than in a final node whose label names the outcome of the failed/re-negotiation branch. Requirement R133 explicitly describes the mediator re-evaluating service requirements and sending them back for re-negotiation, so this branch should not terminate with an unlabeled pass-on final node if it represents the failure outcome within this self-contained module.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R133: 'Else, mediator re-evaluates service requirements and sends to the local PA to perform re-negotiation.' The diagram completes this branch by reaching N18 labeled 'Pass control on' rather than a branch-specific final node naming the failure/re-negotiation outcome.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Use a branch-specific final node for the insufficient-resources outcome, labeled with the outcome name required by the module convention, such as 'Re-negotiation' or 'Insufficient resources', instead of the generic pass-on final node.

final_recommendation: Prioritize D1 first because it is the higher-severity termination defect affecting the long-term peering outcome; address D2 next.
